sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the TrÃ©varesse anticline, in the southern Provence region (SE France), between the towns of Venelles (to the east) and St. Cannat (to the west), just north of Aix-en-Provence. This source lies just south of the E-W trending Cucuron Basin, within the Panneau Provencale.
Recent historical seismicity is intermediate (below Mw 4.7). However, remarkable historical seismicity affected the overall Provence (Champion et al., 2000; Baroux et al, 2001; 2003). In particular, the Mw 5.9 11 June 1909 earthquake affected the area (Baroux et al., 2001, 2003).
The TrÃ©varesse ridge lies above a S-verging reverse fault, active since Miocene times and onwards (Chardon and Bellier, 2003), including a segment associated with the 11 June 1909 earthquake (Mw 5.9; Baroux et al., 2001, 2003).
A segment of this Source has been associated with the key earthquake of this region. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenesis in this region, the reader can refer to the Individual Sources in this Database.
The strike of this Source is based on seismological data. The dip is inferred from seismological data. The rake, indicative of oblique reverse faulting, is inferred from seismological data. The minimum and maximum depth are based on seismological data. The slip rate is based on paleoseismological data.
